This Android phone runs VetrOFF and shares access through its Wi-Fi hotspot. Choose the operating system of the device receiving Wi-Fi. The steps below are for that receiving device, not for this phone.
Root mode is active on this phone. The receiving device should not use a manual proxy.
Wi-Fi gateway of the receiving device
Enable sharing to create a password
On the receiving device, connect to the Wi-Fi hotspot created by this phone and enter the hotspot password. Keep mobile data or another internet connection active on the phone that runs VetrOFF.

Use the phone local IP shown above. Do not enter the remote VPN server address. HTTP and compatible proxy-aware applications can use these settings; applications that ignore the system proxy may connect directly.
Because this phone is using root interception, leave the receiving device proxy set to None / Off. Connect to the hotspot normally and let the phone route client traffic through the VPN.
Simplified settings diagram — menu names can differ by OS version.
Wi-Fi → connected network → Edit → Advanced → Proxy
Settings → Network & internet → Proxy → Manual proxy
System Settings → Network → Wi-Fi → Details → Proxies
Android Wi-Fi settings usually do not provide username/password fields. If the browser does not request credentials, use an application with authenticated HTTP/SOCKS proxy support.
Windows system proxy has limited credential handling. Enter hiddify and the proxy password when the browser or application asks, or configure an authenticated proxy directly in that application.
Desktop environments differ. If the system proxy has no credentials fields, set the authenticated HTTP/SOCKS proxy in the browser or application that should use the VPN.
Enable proxy authentication when available and use username hiddify plus the password shown above.
Turn Authentication on and use username hiddify plus the password shown above.

Open an external IP test on this phone and on the receiving device. For traffic routed through the VPN, the public IP should match. Also test DNS and each application you need because a manual proxy does not capture every protocol.

If the connection times out, confirm the receiving device is still on this phone Wi-Fi, refresh the phone IP, check the port and credentials, and reconnect the VPN after changing sharing settings. HTTP 407 means proxy authentication failed.

If traffic bypasses the VPN, verify root permission on this phone, reconnect the VPN and retry. If root interception is not supported by the device kernel or firmware, disable root mode and use the authenticated proxy method instead.
Disconnect from the phone Wi-Fi and restore Proxy to None / Off on the receiving device. A saved phone IP can prevent internet access on another Wi-Fi network later.
Disconnect from the phone hotspot when finished. No proxy cleanup is required because the receiving device was left on None / Off.

Experimental settings — not recommended for normal use
The options below are intentionally disabled by default. They change application network behavior and may cause compatibility problems. Use them only if you understand the consequences.
These settings are not recommended for normal use. They may break websites, calls, games, local devices, and apps. Continue?
Rejects detected QUIC in user TUN traffic. Browsers usually fall back to HTTPS over TCP, but some apps may lose performance or connectivity.
Rejects detected STUN in the TUN. This can reduce WebRTC network leaks, but may break calls, P2P, games, and media connectivity.
Rejects detected plain HTTP from apps. Non-HTTPS sites, captive portals, and some connectivity checks may stop working.
Rejects TUN application traffic to private LAN addresses. Printers, TVs, routers, NAS devices, and other local services may become unavailable.
A VPN cannot globally change the User-Agent, operating system, browser, Canvas/WebGL, or other data carried inside HTTPS. This mode does not decrypt HTTPS and does not guarantee complete anonymity.
Configure regional app rules, Russian domains and IP ranges, and extra domain rules. Turning a category off preserves its saved selections. App exclusions also depend on your VPN per-app settings.

TCP: AnyTLS and Naive with verified TLS. VLESS/VMess and unverifiable chains are excluded. Requires compatible servers; otherwise connection stops. Masking cannot guarantee bypass of DPI or IP/SNI blocks.

Adds Hysteria 2, TUIC and Naive HTTP/3 to the masked protocol selection. Disable if UDP is blocked. Hysteria obfuscation must match the server. This setting is separate from blocking app QUIC traffic.
Enables adaptive core bandwidth, server selection and longer probe deadlines. The native health check tolerates slower responses and pauses while the underlying network is offline.
The home screen checks internet through the selected core outbound while the app is visible. A failed check does not automatically stop or restart the VPN.

Retry unexpected service failures with bounded backoff while this app is visible. Manual disconnect and VPN permission revocation cancel retries. Adaptive mode also enables recovery.
